Investigation: 18 failed logons against 5 users in 4 minutes followed by a successful login for j.smith. PowerShell execution and an external connection were observed after authentication.
Analyst Notes: Strong password-spray pattern followed by successful authentication and post-login suspicious activity.

Investigation: PowerShell was used to update endpoint security signatures. The command matched an authorized update process and expected administrative activity.
Analyst Notes: Expected security-update activity; no malicious indicators identified.

Investigation: Email contained a suspicious credential-harvesting URL. Link analysis and email indicators showed characteristics consistent with a phishing campaign.
Analyst Notes: Credential-harvesting phishing activity identified.

Investigation: Large transfer matched a scheduled HR backup process and expected internal destination. No suspicious process or external destination was identified.
Analyst Notes: Expected backup activity with legitimate business context.

Investigation: User was added to a privileged group. The change was associated with an authorized administrative activity but required monitoring because of the privileged membership.
Analyst Notes: Authorized privileged-group modification; monitored due to elevated access.

Investigation: Malicious Word document execution led to rundll32 and then PowerShell. The process chain was inconsistent with normal document activity and indicated execution of a suspicious payload.
Analyst Notes: Office-to-rundll32-to-PowerShell process chain indicated malicious execution.

Investigation: SSH activity matched an authorized administrative session. Authentication source and timing were consistent with expected administrator activity.
Analyst Notes: Authorized SSH administration.

Investigation: An automated monitoring script generated an unusual process/deployment event. Activity was verified as an authorized monitoring operation and documented for awareness.
Analyst Notes: Unusual but authorized monitoring activity; documented for future correlation.

Investigation: Web-server exploitation indicators were correlated with DEV-LAPTOP-03 and an outbound connection to port 4444. The behavior was consistent with web-shell or post-exploitation activity.
Analyst Notes: Exploit activity followed by web-shell behavior and outbound command-channel traffic.

Investigation: Periodic DNS and HTTPS activity was observed from WIN-FIN-07 along with hidden PowerShell execution. Timing and process/network correlation were consistent with C2 beaconing.
Analyst Notes: Periodic communications and hidden PowerShell indicated possible command-and-control activity.

Investigation: DNS requests matched the legitimate DataSync Agent and expected telemetry infrastructure. Frequency and destination were consistent with normal application behavior.
Analyst Notes: Legitimate application telemetry.

Investigation: Cloud traffic matched normal SalesSync CRM communication. Destination, timing, and application context were consistent with authorized business activity.
Analyst Notes: Legitimate CRM cloud traffic; retained for monitoring.

Investigation: A 1.7 GB upload to an external legal file-share was investigated. The destination was an approved corporate file-share, external counsel was involved, and the transfer was associated with an approved document manager/sync application with no malware indicators.
Analyst Notes: Large transfer was authorized and supported by business context.

Investigation: EDR detected svchost.exe from the user's AppData path. Explorer launched the executable, followed by hidden encoded PowerShell. A malicious unsigned hash, Registry Run key persistence, and periodic outbound HTTPS to an unapproved destination were confirmed.
Analyst Notes: Malicious executable path/hash, encoded PowerShell, persistence, and repeated external communication.

Investigation: RemoteSupportUpdater and rsupdate.exe ran as LocalSystem. Change ticket CHG-2026-1001-042, signed vendor binary/hash, approved endpoint, and absence of suspicious child processes confirmed authorized activity.
Analyst Notes: Legitimate remote-support service with approved change context.

Investigation: Explorer launched rundll32 with invoice.dll after a malicious Excel document. Hidden PowerShell downloaded update.ps1 from unapproved infrastructure and created a scheduled task named WindowsUpdateCheck.
Analyst Notes: Malicious DLL execution, PowerShell download, scheduled-task persistence, and external communication.

Investigation: ProcDump was used to dump LSASS memory, producing a large dump that was compressed into debug.zip. The activity followed an unapproved external document and included an attempted outbound connection with no legitimate ticket.
Analyst Notes: Credential-dumping behavior with archive creation and suspicious outbound communication.

Investigation: Collect-SystemInfo.ps1 used ExecutionPolicy Bypass but was signed by the company IT certificate, matched the approved repository/hash, and ran from the scheduled IT-SystemInventory task under approved ticket CHG-2026-1001-061.
Analyst Notes: ExecutionPolicy Bypass was present but fully supported by authorized IT context.

Investigation: Fourteen failed logons occurred in 4 minutes followed by successful Logon Type 10 authentication. Source 10.10.40.72 belonged to LAPTOP-22 assigned to another user, and WIN-FIN-15 then accessed WIN-FILE-03 over SMB.
Analyst Notes: Authentication anomaly plus unexpected source endpoint and subsequent SMB access indicated compromise.

Investigation: Word document execution spawned PowerShell and a second PowerShell process with hidden encoded Bypass. update.ps1 was downloaded from external infrastructure, a scheduled task was created, and an HR salary file was targeted.
Analyst Notes: Malicious document, encoded PowerShell, download, persistence, and sensitive-file targeting.

Investigation: Account a.joshi was added to local Administrators without a ticket. PowerShell enumerated users/groups, whoami was executed, the built-in Administrator account was enabled, and a suspicious Temp PowerShell script plus external HTTPS traffic were observed.
Analyst Notes: Unauthorized privilege change correlated with discovery, account enablement, suspicious script, and network activity.

Investigation: Three failed RDP attempts were followed by a successful Logon Type 10 session. The source was WIN-ACCT-03. The user confirmed approved IT support activity under ticket IT-2026-1048, with no suspicious PowerShell, credential access, external traffic, or file transfer.
Analyst Notes: RDP activity was authorized and explained by an IT support ticket.

Investigation: Invoice_2026_10_05.exe launched cmd and hidden PowerShell. The script downloaded a.ps1 from unapproved infrastructure, created a scheduled task for persistence, made outbound HTTPS connections, accessed browser credential files, and matched a known malicious sample.
Analyst Notes: Malware execution, download, persistence, C2-like traffic, and browser credential access.

Investigation: 1.4 GB was transferred to unapproved cloud storage after access to 320 Legal files, including confidential case and settlement documents. DLP confirmed the transfer, no ticket existed, and management confirmed the activity was unauthorized.
Analyst Notes: Large sensitive-data transfer to unapproved cloud storage; no malware was identified.

Investigation: Explorer launched PowerShell followed by rundll32 and an unsigned cred.dll from Temp. The DLL accessed SAM-related credential data, connected externally, had malicious reputation, and was followed by successful internal authentication.
Analyst Notes: Malicious DLL, credential-store access, external communication, and subsequent authentication supported compromise.

Investigation: Successful authentication occurred to WIN-APP-02, WIN-DB-04, and WIN-FILE-07 after seven failures. The failures were caused by an old password, and IT ticket DEV-2026-1087 plus manager confirmation established authorized database and file-share access.
Analyst Notes: Internal activity was explained by an approved development troubleshooting task.

Investigation: Successful cloud login occurred from an unfamiliar IP and unregistered device. MFA succeeded, but VPN logs showed no session, the user's registered laptop was active on the corporate network, and 12 internal financial documents were downloaded. The user denied approving the login.
Analyst Notes: Compromised cloud identity suspected based on anomalous login, unregistered device, and unauthorized sensitive downloads.

Investigation: Explorer launched hidden PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass. update-check.ps1 was placed in AppData and launched by a user-created scheduled task every 30 minutes. The script was unsigned, downloaded config.ps1 from malicious infrastructure, and performed system/network discovery.
Analyst Notes: Encoded/hidden PowerShell, persistence, malicious download, and discovery activity with no approved business context.

Investigation: Nmap -sS -sV scanned 10.10.20.0/24, contacting 42 hosts and about 1,200 connections across common service ports. User cited application testing, but no security/change ticket existed and production-adjacent systems were included.
Analyst Notes: Scanning was not pre-approved and exceeded normal scope, but no exploitation or malicious endpoint activity was observed.

Investigation: Expired admin-temp credentials were used from WIN-IT-07 to create backup-admin and add it to Domain Admins. Events 4720 and 4728 confirmed account creation and privileged-group membership. The new account authenticated to additional domain systems with no approved ticket.
Analyst Notes: Unauthorized privileged account creation and Domain Admin membership followed by additional authentication.

Investigation: svc-reporting executed 4,800 SELECT queries in 8 minutes and returned 2.3 GB of sensitive customer, payment, and transaction data outside the normal 02:00 report schedule. The reporting task had been moved to 16:00 without a ticket, query scope exceeded normal reporting, and WIN-APP-02 subsequently made unapproved HTTPS traffic to external infrastructure.
Analyst Notes: Legitimate reporting process was abused through unauthorized schedule and scope changes, followed by suspicious outbound transfer activity.
